name: Unicode Fullwidth ASCII variant
description:
Summary:
This event is generated when an attempt is made to evade detection of the attack. This is a general detection signature (i.e. it is not specific to any web application).

--
Impact:
Vary from information gathering to web server compromise.

--
Detailed Information:
This event is generated when an attempt is made to evade detection of the attack on a web server, by obfuscating the attack using various methods such as encodings, path manipulation, and others.

--
Affected Systems:
All systems.

--
Attack Scenarios:
There are many possible.

--
Ease of Attack:
Simple to medium.

--
False Positives:
Some applications may accept valid input which matches these signatures.

--
False Negatives:
None known.

--
Corrective Action:
Ensure the system is using an up to date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied. 
Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

--
Additional References:



--

name: Gitea Code Injection
description:
Summary:
This event is generated when an attempt is made to inject Server-side Include code. This is a general attack detection signature (i.e. it is not specific to any web application).

Impact:
Serious. Execution of arbitrary commands may be possible.

Detailed Information:
This event indicates that an attempt has been made to inject Server-side Include (SSI) code. SSI Injection allows to attacker to send server side code that could be executed locally by the web server.

Affected Systems:
All systems.

Attack Scenarios:
There are many possible.

Ease Of Attack:
Simple to medium.

False Positives:
Some applications may accept valid input which matches these signatures.

False Negatives:
None known.

Corrective Action:
Ensure the system is using an up to date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied. Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

name: WordPress Unauthenticated XSS
description:
Summary:
This event is generated when an attempt is made to exploit a Cross Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability. This is a general attack detection signature (i.e. it is not specific to any web application).

Impact:
Successful exploitation will result in information gathering and system integrity compromise. Possible unauthorized administrative access to the server or application can result. Possible execution of arbitrary code of the attacker's choosing can result.

Detailed Information:
This event indicates that an attempt has been made to exploit a Cross Site Scripting vulnerability in an application running on a webserver.Cross Site Scripting (XSS) occurs when a web application doesn't sanitize user-supplied input and places it directly into the page returned to the user. Usually the attacker will submit malicious JavaScript, VBScript, ActiveX, HTML, or Flash code to the vulnerable web site.

Affected Systems:
All systems that accept user input are potentially affected.

Attack Scenarios:
An attacker can supply a malicious link designed to steal information from a user clicking on that link.

Ease Of Attack:
Vary from simple to medium.

False Positives:
Some applications send various script code to the web server as legitimate input.Some free-text user input may match Cross Site Scripting signatures.

False Negatives:
None known.

Corrective Action:
Ensure the system is using an up to date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied.Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

Additional References:
http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross_site_scripting
http://www.cgisecurity.com/articles/xss-faq.shtml

This event is generated when an attempt is made to exploit a Cross Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability. This is a general attack detection signature (i.e. it is not specific to any web application).

Impact:
Successful exploitation will result in information gathering and system integrity compromise. Possible unauthorized administrative access to the server or application can result. Possible execution of arbitrary code of the attacker's choosing can result.

Detailed Information:
This event indicates that an attempt has been made to exploit a Cross Site Scripting vulnerability in an application running on a webserver.Cross Site Scripting (XSS) occurs when a web application doesn't sanitize user-supplied input and places it directly into the page returned to the user. Usually the attacker will submit malicious JavaScript, VBScript, ActiveX, HTML, or Flash code to the vulnerable web site.

Affected Systems:
All systems that accept user input are potentially affected.

Attack Scenarios:
An attacker can supply a malicious link designed to steal information from a user clicking on that link.

Ease Of Attack:
Vary from simple to medium.

False Positives:
Some applications send various script code to the web server as legitimate input.Some free-text user input may match Cross Site Scripting signatures.

False Negatives:
None known.

Corrective Action:
Ensure the system is using an up to date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied.Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

Additional References:
http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross_site_scripting
http://www.cgisecurity.com/articles/xss-faq.shtml

Summary:
This event is generated when an attempt is made to inject Server-side Include code. This is a general attack detection signature (i.e. it is not specific to any web application).

Impact:
Serious. Execution of arbitrary commands may be possible.

Detailed Information:
This event indicates that an attempt has been made to inject Server-side Include (SSI) code. SSI Injection allows to attacker to send server side code that could be executed locally by the web server.

Affected Systems:
All systems.

Attack Scenarios:
There are many possible.

Ease Of Attack:
Simple to medium.

False Positives:
Some applications may accept valid input which matches these signatures.

False Negatives:
None known.

Corrective Action:
Ensure the system is using an up to date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied. Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

Additional References:
http://www.webappsec.org/projects/threat/classes/ssi_injection.shtml

Serious. Execution of arbitrary commands may be possible.

This event indicates that an attempt has been made to inject Server-side Include (SSI) code. SSI Injection allows to attacker to send server side code that could be executed locally by the web server.

Affected Systems:
All systems.

There are many possible.

Simple to medium.

Some applications may accept valid input which matches these signatures.

None known.

This event is generated when an attempt is made to inject Server-side Include code. This is a general attack detection signature (i.e. it is not specific to any web application).

Impact:
Serious. Execution of arbitrary commands may be possible.

Detailed Information:
This event indicates that an attempt has been made to inject Server-side Include (SSI) code. SSI Injection allows to attacker to send server side code that could be executed locally by the web server.

Affected Systems:
All systems.

Attack Scenarios:
There are many possible.

Ease Of Attack:
Simple to medium.

False Positives:
Some applications may accept valid input which matches these signatures.

False Negatives:
None known.

Ensure the system is using an up to date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied. Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

Additional References:
http://www.webappsec.org/projects/threat/classes/ssi_injection.shtml

This event is generated when an attempt is made to inject Server-side Include code. This is a general attack detection signature (i.e. it is not specific to any web application).

Impact:
Serious. Execution of arbitrary commands may be possible.

Detailed Information:
This event indicates that an attempt has been made to inject Server-side Include (SSI) code. SSI Injection allows to attacker to send server side code that could be executed locally by the web server.

Affected Systems:
All systems.

Attack Scenarios:
There are many possible.

Ease Of Attack:
Simple to medium.

False Positives:
Some applications may accept valid input which matches these signatures.

False Negatives:
None known.

Corrective Action:
Ensure the system is using an up to date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied. Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

Additional References:
http://www.webappsec.org/projects/threat/classes/ssi_injection.shtml

Summary:
This event is generated when an attempt is made to inject Server-side Include code. This is a general attack detection signature (i.e. it is not specific to any web application).

Impact:
Serious. Execution of arbitrary commands may be possible.

Detailed Information:
This event indicates that an attempt has been made to inject Server-side Include (SSI) code. SSI Injection allows to attacker to send server side code that could be executed locally by the web server.

Affected Systems:
All systems.

Attack Scenarios:
There are many possible.

Ease Of Attack:
Simple to medium.

False Positives:
Some applications may accept valid input which matches these signatures.

False Negatives:
None known.

Corrective Action:
Ensure the system is using an up to date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied. Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

Additional References:
http://www.webappsec.org/projects/threat/classes/ssi_injection.shtml

This event is generated when an attempt is made to remotely execute an OS command. This is a general attack detection signature (i.e. it is not specific to any web application, but is dependent on the webserver Operating System).

Serious. Execution of arbitrary commands may be possible.

Web application could be tricked to execute operating system command if user supplied input isn't properly checked. This event indicates that an attempt has been made to inject an operating system command from a remote machine via unvalidated input of web application.

Affected Systems:
All systems.

Attack Scenarios:
There are many possible.

Ease Of Attack:
Simple to medium.

False Positives:
Some applications may accept valid input which matches these signatures.

False Negatives:
None known.

Ensure the system is using an up to date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied. Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

This event is generated when an attempt is made to remotely execute an OS command. This is a general attack detection signature (i.e. it is not specific to any web application, but is dependent on the webserver Operating System).

Impact:
Serious. Execution of arbitrary commands may be possible.

Detailed Information:
Web application could be tricked to execute operating system command if user supplied input isn't properly checked. This event indicates that an attempt has been made to inject an operating system command from a remote machine via unvalidated input of web application.

Affected Systems:
All systems.

Attack Scenarios:
There are many possible.

Ease Of Attack:
Simple to medium.

False Positives:
Some applications may accept valid input which matches these signatures.

False Negatives:
None known.

Corrective Action:
Ensure the system is using an up to date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied. Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

Additional References:
http://www.webappsec.org/projects/threat/classes/os_commanding.shtml

name: NocoBase SQL Injection
description:
Summary:
This event is generated when an attempt is made to exploit an SQL-Injection vulnerability. This is a general attack detection signature (i.e. it is not specific to any database or web application).

Impact:
Successful exploitation will result in information gathering and system integrity compromise. Possible unauthorized administrative access to the server or application can result. Possible execution of arbitrary code of the attacker's choosing can result.

Detailed Information:
SQL-Injection occurs when a web application doesn't sanitize user-supplied input and places it directly into the SQL statement. This event indicates that an attempt has been made by the client to inject SQL code into the application.

Affected Systems:
All systems with database connectivity are potentially affected.

Attack Scenarios:
An attacker can inject SQL commands to the backend database for an application if user input is not correctly sanitized or checked before passing that input to the database.

Ease Of Attack:
Vary from simple to medium.

False Positives:
Some applications send SQL statements to the web server as legitimate input. Some free-text user input may match SQL-Injection signatures.

False Negatives:
None known.

Corrective Action:
Ensure the system is using an up to date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied.Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

Additional References:

None known.

Successful exploitation will result in information gathering and system integrity compromise. Possible unauthorized administrative access to the server or application can result. Possible execution of arbitrary code of the attacker's choosing can result.

Detailed Information:
SQL-Injection occurs when a web application doesn't sanitize user-supplied input and places it directly into the SQL statement. This event indicates that an attempt has been made by the client to inject SQL code into the application.

Affected Systems:
All systems with database connectivity are potentially affected.

Attack Scenarios:
An attacker can inject SQL commands to the backend database for an application if user input is not correctly sanitized or checked before passing that input to the database.

Ease Of Attack:
Vary from simple to medium.

False Positives:
Some applications send SQL statements to the web server as legitimate input. Some free-text user input may match SQL-Injection signatures.

False Negatives:
None known.

Corrective Action:
Ensure the system is using an up to date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied.Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

name: SQL-INJ convert_from (URI)
description:
Summary:
This event is generated when an attempt is made to exploit an SQL-Injection vulnerability. This is a general attack detection signature (i.e. it is not specific to any database or web application).

Impact:
Successful exploitation will result in information gathering and system integrity compromise. Possible unauthorized administrative access to the server or application can result. Possible execution of arbitrary code of the attacker's choosing can result.

Detailed Information:
SQL-Injection occurs when a web application doesn't sanitize user-supplied input and places it directly into the SQL statement. This event indicates that an attempt has been made by the client to inject SQL code into the application.

Affected Systems:
All systems with database connectivity are potentially affected.

Attack Scenarios:
An attacker can inject SQL commands to the backend database for an application if user input is not correctly sanitized or checked before passing that input to the database.

Ease Of Attack:
Vary from simple to medium.

False Positives:
Some applications send SQL statements to the web server as legitimate input. Some free-text user input may match SQL-Injection signatures.

False Negatives:
None known.

Corrective Action:
Ensure the system is using an up to date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied.Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

Additional References:
http://www.webappsec.org/projects/threat/classes/sql_injection.shtml

Successful exploitation will result in information gathering and system integrity compromise. Possible unauthorized administrative access to the server or application can result. Possible execution of arbitrary code of the attacker's choosing can result.

Detailed Information:
This event indicates that an attempt has been made to exploit a Cross Site Scripting vulnerability in an application running on a webserver.Cross Site Scripting (XSS) occurs when a web application doesn't sanitize user-supplied input and places it directly into the page returned to the user. Usually the attacker will submit malicious JavaScript, VBScript, ActiveX, HTML, or Flash code to the vulnerable web site.

Affected Systems:
All systems that accept user input are potentially affected.

Attack Scenarios:
An attacker can supply a malicious link designed to steal information from a user clicking on that link.

Ease Of Attack:
Vary from simple to medium.

False Positives:
Some applications send various script code to the web server as legitimate input.Some free-text user input may match Cross Site Scripting signatures.

False Negatives:
None known.

Corrective Action:
Ensure the system is using an up to date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied.Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

Additional References:
http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross_site_scripting
http://www.cgisecurity.com/articles/xss-faq.shtml

Successful exploitation will result in information gathering and system integrity compromise. Possible unauthorized administrative access to the server or application can result. Possible execution of arbitrary code of the attacker's choosing can result.

Detailed Information:
This event indicates that an attempt has been made to exploit a Cross Site Scripting vulnerability in an application running on a webserver.Cross Site Scripting (XSS) occurs when a web application doesn't sanitize user-supplied input and places it directly into the page returned to the user. Usually the attacker will submit malicious JavaScript, VBScript, ActiveX, HTML, or Flash code to the vulnerable web site.

Affected Systems:
All systems that accept user input are potentially affected.

An attacker can supply a malicious link designed to steal information from a user clicking on that link.

False Positives:
Some applications send various script code to the web server as legitimate input.Some free-text user input may match Cross Site Scripting signatures.

False Negatives:
None known.

Corrective Action:
Ensure the system is using an up to date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied.Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

All systems that accept user input are potentially affected.

An attacker can supply a malicious link designed to steal information from a user clicking on that link.

Some applications send various script code to the web server as legitimate input.Some free-text user input may match Cross Site Scripting signatures.

False Negatives:
None known.

Ensure the system is using an up to date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied.Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

This event is generated when an attempt is made to exploit a Cross Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability. This is a general attack detection signature (i.e. it is not specific to any web application).

Impact:
Successful exploitation will result in information gathering and system integrity compromise. Possible unauthorized administrative access to the server or application can result. Possible execution of arbitrary code of the attacker's choosing can result.

Detailed Information:
This event indicates that an attempt has been made to exploit a Cross Site Scripting vulnerability in an application running on a webserver.Cross Site Scripting (XSS) occurs when a web application doesn't sanitize user-supplied input and places it directly into the page returned to the user. Usually the attacker will submit malicious JavaScript, VBScript, ActiveX, HTML, or Flash code to the vulnerable web site.

Affected Systems:
All systems that accept user input are potentially affected.

Attack Scenarios:
An attacker can supply a malicious link designed to steal information from a user clicking on that link.

Ease Of Attack:
Vary from simple to medium.

False Positives:
Some applications send various script code to the web server as legitimate input.Some free-text user input may match Cross Site Scripting signatures.

False Negatives:
None known.

Corrective Action:
Ensure the system is using an up to date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied.Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

Additional References:
http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross_site_scripting
http://www.cgisecurity.com/articles/xss-faq.shtml

name: setInterval() (URI)
description:
Summary:
This event is generated when an attempt is made to exploit a Cross Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability. This is a general attack detection signature (i.e. it is not specific to any web application).

Impact:
Successful exploitation will result in information gathering and system integrity compromise. Possible unauthorized administrative access to the server or application can result. Possible execution of arbitrary code of the attacker's choosing can result.

Detailed Information:
This event indicates that an attempt has been made to exploit a Cross Site Scripting vulnerability in an application running on a webserver.Cross Site Scripting (XSS) occurs when a web application doesn't sanitize user-supplied input and places it directly into the page returned to the user. Usually the attacker will submit malicious JavaScript, VBScript, ActiveX, HTML, or Flash code to the vulnerable web site.

Affected Systems:
All systems that accept user input are potentially affected.

Attack Scenarios:
An attacker can supply a malicious link designed to steal information from a user clicking on that link.

Ease Of Attack:
Vary from simple to medium.

False Positives:
Some applications send various script code to the web server as legitimate input.Some free-text user input may match Cross Site Scripting signatures.

False Negatives:
None known.

Corrective Action:
Ensure the system is using an up to date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied.Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

Additional References:
http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross_site_scripting
http://www.cgisecurity.com/articles/xss-faq.shtml

Successful exploitation will result in information gathering and system integrity compromise. Possible unauthorized administrative access to the server or application can result. Possible execution of arbitrary code of the attacker's choosing can result.

Detailed Information:
This event indicates that an attempt has been made to exploit a Cross Site Scripting vulnerability in an application running on a webserver.Cross Site Scripting (XSS) occurs when a web application doesn't sanitize user-supplied input and places it directly into the page returned to the user. Usually the attacker will submit malicious JavaScript, VBScript, ActiveX, HTML, or Flash code to the vulnerable web site.

Affected Systems:
All systems that accept user input are potentially affected.

Attack Scenarios:
An attacker can supply a malicious link designed to steal information from a user clicking on that link.

Ease Of Attack:
Vary from simple to medium.

False Positives:
Some applications send various script code to the web server as legitimate input.Some free-text user input may match Cross Site Scripting signatures.

False Negatives:
None known.

Corrective Action:
Ensure the system is using an up to date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied.Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

Additional References:
http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross_site_scripting
http://www.cgisecurity.com/articles/xss-faq.shtml

name: Ember.js run (URI)
description:
Summary:
This event is generated when an attempt is made to exploit a Cross Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability. This is a general attack detection signature (i.e. it is not specific to any web application).

Impact:
Successful exploitation will result in information gathering and system integrity compromise. Possible unauthorized administrative access to the server or application can result. Possible execution of arbitrary code of the attacker's choosing can result.

Detailed Information:
This event indicates that an attempt has been made to exploit a Cross Site Scripting vulnerability in an application running on a webserver.Cross Site Scripting (XSS) occurs when a web application doesn't sanitize user-supplied input and places it directly into the page returned to the user. Usually the attacker will submit malicious JavaScript, VBScript, ActiveX, HTML, or Flash code to the vulnerable web site.

Affected Systems:
All systems that accept user input are potentially affected.

Attack Scenarios:
An attacker can supply a malicious link designed to steal information from a user clicking on that link.

Ease Of Attack:
Vary from simple to medium.

False Positives:
Some applications send various script code to the web server as legitimate input.Some free-text user input may match Cross Site Scripting signatures.

False Negatives:
None known.

Corrective Action:
Ensure the system is using an up to date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied.Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

Additional References:
http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross_site_scripting
http://www.cgisecurity.com/articles/xss-faq.shtml

This event is generated when an attempt is made to exploit a Cross Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability. This is a general attack detection signature (i.e. it is not specific to any web application).

Impact:
Successful exploitation will result in information gathering and system integrity compromise. Possible unauthorized administrative access to the server or application can result. Possible execution of arbitrary code of the attacker's choosing can result.

Detailed Information:
This event indicates that an attempt has been made to exploit a Cross Site Scripting vulnerability in an application running on a webserver.Cross Site Scripting (XSS) occurs when a web application doesn't sanitize user-supplied input and places it directly into the page returned to the user. Usually the attacker will submit malicious JavaScript, VBScript, ActiveX, HTML, or Flash code to the vulnerable web site.

Affected Systems:
All systems that accept user input are potentially affected.

Attack Scenarios:
An attacker can supply a malicious link designed to steal information from a user clicking on that link.

Ease Of Attack:
Vary from simple to medium.

False Positives:
Some applications send various script code to the web server as legitimate input.Some free-text user input may match Cross Site Scripting signatures.

False Negatives:
None known.

Corrective Action:
Ensure the system is using an up to date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied.Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

Additional References:
http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross_site_scripting
http://www.cgisecurity.com/articles/xss-faq.shtml

name: self[] (URI)
description:
Summary:
This event is generated when an attempt is made to exploit a Cross Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability. This is a general attack detection signature (i.e. it is not specific to any web application).

Impact:
Successful exploitation will result in information gathering and system integrity compromise. Possible unauthorized administrative access to the server or application can result. Possible execution of arbitrary code of the attacker's choosing can result.

Detailed Information:
This event indicates that an attempt has been made to exploit a Cross Site Scripting vulnerability in an application running on a webserver.Cross Site Scripting (XSS) occurs when a web application doesn't sanitize user-supplied input and places it directly into the page returned to the user. Usually the attacker will submit malicious JavaScript, VBScript, ActiveX, HTML, or Flash code to the vulnerable web site.

Affected Systems:
All systems that accept user input are potentially affected.

Attack Scenarios:
An attacker can supply a malicious link designed to steal information from a user clicking on that link.

Ease Of Attack:
Vary from simple to medium.

False Positives:
Some applications send various script code to the web server as legitimate input.Some free-text user input may match Cross Site Scripting signatures.

False Negatives:
None known.

Corrective Action:
Ensure the system is using an up to date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied.Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

Additional References:
http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross_site_scripting
http://www.cgisecurity.com/articles/xss-faq.shtml

None known.

name: esi tag (Parameter)
description:
Summary:
This event is generated when an attempt is made to exploit a Cross Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability. This is a general attack detection signature (i.e. it is not specific to any web application).

Impact:
Successful exploitation will result in information gathering and system integrity compromise. Possible unauthorized administrative access to the server or application can result. Possible execution of arbitrary code of the attacker's choosing can result.

Detailed Information:
This event indicates that an attempt has been made to exploit a Cross Site Scripting vulnerability in an application running on a webserver.Cross Site Scripting (XSS) occurs when a web application doesn't sanitize user-supplied input and places it directly into the page returned to the user. Usually the attacker will submit malicious JavaScript, VBScript, ActiveX, HTML, or Flash code to the vulnerable web site.

Affected Systems:
All systems that accept user input are potentially affected.

Attack Scenarios:
An attacker can supply a malicious link designed to steal information from a user clicking on that link.

Ease Of Attack:
Vary from simple to medium.

False Positives:
Some applications send various script code to the web server as legitimate input.Some free-text user input may match Cross Site Scripting signatures.

False Negatives:
None known.

Corrective Action:
Ensure the system is using an up to date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied.Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

Additional References:
http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross_site_scripting
http://www.cgisecurity.com/articles/xss-faq.shtml

Affected Systems:
All systems.

There are many possible.

Ease Of Attack:
Simple to medium.

False Positives:
Some applications may accept valid input which matches these signatures.

None known.

name: console.trace (Parameter)
description:
Summary:
This event is generated when an attempt is made to exploit a Cross Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability. This is a general attack detection signature (i.e. it is not specific to any web application).

Impact:
 Successful exploitation will result in information gathering and system integrity compromise. Possible unauthorized administrative access to the server or application can result. Possible execution of arbitrary code of the attacker's choosing can result.

Detailed Information:
This event indicates that an attempt has been made to exploit a Cross Site Scripting vulnerability in an application running on a webserver. Cross Site Scripting (XSS) occurs when a web application doesn't sanitize user-supplied input and places it directly into the page returned to the user. Usually the attacker will submit malicious JavaScript, VBScript, ActiveX, HTML, or Flash code to the vulnerable web site.

Affected Systems:
All systems that accept user input are potentially affected.

Attack Scenarios:
An attacker can supply a malicious link designed to steal information from a user clicking on that link.

Ease Of Attack:
Vary from simple to medium.

False Positives:
Some applications send various script code to the web server as legitimate input.Some free-text user input may match Cross Site Scripting signatures.

False Negatives:
None known.

Corrective Action:
Ensure the system is using an up-to-date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied. Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

Additional References:
http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross_site_scripting
http://www.cgisecurity.com/articles/xss-faq.shtml

description:

There are many possible.

Simple to medium.

Some applications may accept valid input which matches these signatures.

None known.

name: XSS script tag with namespace (URI)
description:
Summary:
This event is generated when an attempt is made to exploit a Cross Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability. This is a general attack detection signature (i.e. it is not specific to any web application).

Impact:
Successful exploitation will result in information gathering and system integrity compromise. Possible unauthorized administrative access to the server or application can result. Possible execution of arbitrary code of the attacker's choosing can result.

Detailed Information:
This event indicates that an attempt has been made to exploit a Cross Site Scripting vulnerability in an application running on a webserver.Cross Site Scripting (XSS) occurs when a web application doesn't sanitize user-supplied input and places it directly into the page returned to the user. Usually the attacker will submit malicious JavaScript, VBScript, ActiveX, HTML, or Flash code to the vulnerable web site.

Affected Systems:
All systems that accept user input are potentially affected.

Attack Scenarios:
An attacker can supply a malicious link designed to steal information from a user clicking on that link.

Ease Of Attack:
Vary from simple to medium.

False Positives:
Some applications send various script code to the web server as legitimate input.Some free-text user input may match Cross Site Scripting signatures.

False Negatives:
None known.

Corrective Action:
Ensure the system is using an up to date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied.Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

Additional References:
http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross_site_scripting
http://www.cgisecurity.com/articles/xss-faq.shtml

Successful exploitation will result in information gathering and system integrity compromise. Possible unauthorized administrative access to the server or application can result. Possible execution of arbitrary code of the attacker's choosing can result.

Detailed Information:
This event indicates that an attempt has been made to exploit a Cross Site Scripting vulnerability in an application running on a webserver. Cross Site Scripting (XSS) occurs when a web application doesn't sanitize user-supplied input and places it directly into the page returned to the user. Usually the attacker will submit malicious JavaScript, VBScript, ActiveX, HTML, or Flash code to the vulnerable web site.

Affected Systems:
All systems that accept user input are potentially affected.

Attack Scenarios:
An attacker can supply a malicious link designed to steal information from a user clicking on that link.

Ease Of Attack:
Vary from simple to medium.

False Positives:
Some applications send various script code to the web server as legitimate input.Some free-text user input may match Cross Site Scripting signatures.

False Negatives:
None known.

Corrective Action:
Ensure the system is using an up-to-date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied. Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

name: onvoicechange (URI)
description:
Summary:
This event is triggered when an attempt is made to inject code via an HTML tag attribute.

Impact:
Vary from information gathering to web server compromise.

Detailed Information:
This event is triggered when an attempt is made to exploit an open HTML tag, and insert a JavaScript command via a JavaScript event attribute.

Affected Systems:
All systems

Attack Scenarios:
There are many possible.

Ease Of Attack:
Simple to medium.

False Positives:
Some applications may accept valid input which matches these signatures.

False Negatives:
None known.

Corrective Action:
Make sure the application writes HTML tags that are properly closed.
Make sure the application properly sanitizes user input that is being used to generate HTML.

This event is triggered when an attempt is made to inject code via an HTML tag attribute.

Impact:
Vary from information gathering to web server compromise.

Detailed Information:
This event is triggered when an attempt is made to exploit an open HTML tag, and insert a JavaScript command via a JavaScript event attribute.

Affected Systems:
All systems

Attack Scenarios:
There are many possible.

Ease Of Attack:
Simple to medium.

False Positives:
Some applications may accept valid input which matches these signatures.

False Negatives:
None known.

Corrective Action:
Make sure the application writes HTML tags that are properly closed.
Make sure the application properly sanitizes user input that is being used to generate HTML.

Additional References:
http://www.owasp.org/index.php/XSS_Filter_Evasion_Cheat_Sheet#Event_Handlers

This event is triggered when an attempt is made to inject code via an HTML tag attribute.

Impact:
Vary from information gathering to web server compromise.

Detailed Information:
This event is triggered when an attempt is made to exploit an open HTML tag, and insert a JavaScript command via a JavaScript event attribute.

Affected Systems:
All systems

Attack Scenarios:
There are many possible.

Ease Of Attack:
Simple to medium.

False Positives:
Some applications may accept valid input which matches these signatures.

False Negatives:
None known.

Corrective Action:
Make sure the application writes HTML tags that are properly closed.
Make sure the application properly sanitizes user input that is being used to generate HTML.

Additional References:
http://www.owasp.org/index.php/XSS_Filter_Evasion_Cheat_Sheet#Event_Handlers

name: XSLT Code Execution inside SOAP Signature
description:
Summary:
This event is generated when an attempt is made to remotely execute commands using XSLT mechanism. Web services standard WS-* allows usage of XSLT mechanism as a transformation algorithm for digitally signing the message.

--
Impact:
Serious. Execution of arbitrary commands may be possible.

description:
Summary:
This event is generated when an attempt is made to access hidden web site content or functionality. This is a general detection signature (i.e. it is not specific to any web application).

--
Impact:
Information disclosure. This may aid the attacker to mount a more dangerous attack.

--
Detailed Information:
By making educated guesses, the attacker could discover hidden web site content and functionality, such as configuration, temporary, backup or sample files.
This can lead to the disclosure of sensitive system information which may
be used by an attacker to further compromise the system.

--
Affected Systems:
All systems.

--
Attack Scenarios:
An attacker can search the web site for known sample files or files with .tmp, .bak and other extensions or attempt to access administrative pages or directories.

--
Ease of Attack:
Simple.

--
False Positives:
None known.

--
False Negatives:
None known.

--

This event is generated when an attempt is made to obtain sensitive information or a leakage has been detected. This is a general detection signature (i.e. it is not specific to any web application).

--
Impact:
Information disclosure.
The information may be sensitive itself (e.g. credit card numbers) or  may aid the attacker to mount a more dangerous attack (e.g. user or system passwords).

--
Detailed Information:
Sensitive information may be present within HTML comments, error messages, source code, or simply left in files which are accessible by remote clients.
This can lead to the disclosure of sensitive system information which may
be used by an attacker to further compromise the system.

--
Affected Systems:
All systems.

--
Attack Scenarios:
An attacker can search HTML files for comments, send unexpected requests to generate error messages or access to sensitive files.

--
Ease of Attack:
Simple.

--
False Positives:
None known.

--
False Negatives:
None known.

--
Corrective Action:
Ensure the system is using an up to date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied. Disallow access to sensitive files, remove any comments left in the user accessible code.
Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

--
Additional References:

Information Leakage
http://www.webappsec.org/projects/threat/classes/information_leakage.shtml

name: php.exe access
description:
Summary:
This event is generated when an attempt is made to remotely execute an OS command. This is a general attack detection signature (i.e. it is not specific to any web application, but is dependent on the webserver Operating System).

--
Impact:
Serious. Execution of arbitrary commands may be possible.

--
Detailed Information:
Web application could be tricked to execute operating system command if user supplied input isn't properly checked.
This event indicates that an attempt has been made to inject an operating system command from a remote machine via unvalidated input of web application.

--
Affected Systems:
PHP versions 4.3.0 and prior used on Apache web servers for windows.

--
Attack Scenarios:
Read file: http://[targethost]/php/php.exe?c:\filetoread
Execute file: http://[targethost]/php/php.exe?c:\filetoexecute

--
Ease of Attack:
Vary from simple to medium.

--
False Positives:
Some free-text user input may match Command Execution signatures.

--
False Negatives:
None known.

--
Corrective Action:
Ensure the system is using an up to date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied.
Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

This event is generated when an attempt is made to remotely execute an OS command. This is a general attack detection signature (i.e. it is not specific to any web application, but is dependent on the webserver Operating System).

--
Impact:
Serious. Execution of arbitrary commands may be possible.

--
Detailed Information:
Web application could be tricked to execute operating system command if user supplied input isn't properly checked.
This event indicates that an attempt has been made to inject an operating system command from a remote machine via unvalidated input of web application.

--
Affected Systems:
All systems.

--
Attack Scenarios:
An attacker can supply or invoke execution of OS commands via unsanitized input.

--
Ease of Attack:
Vary from simple to medium.

--
False Positives:
Some free-text user input may match Command Execution signatures.

--
False Negatives:
None known.

--
Corrective Action:
Ensure the system is using an up to date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied.
Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

--

OS Commanding

name: Malicious Web Site crawler "x-aaaaaa"
description:
Summary:
This event is generated when an attempt is made to obtain sensitive information or a leakage has been detected. This is a general detection signature (i.e. it is not specific to any web application).

--
Impact:
Information disclosure.
The information may be sensitive itself (e.g. credit card numbers) or  may aid the attacker to mount a more dangerous attack (e.g. user or system passwords).

--
Detailed Information:
Sensitive information may be present within HTML comments, error messages, source code, or simply left in files which are accessible by remote clients.
This can lead to the disclosure of sensitive system information which may
be used by an attacker to further compromise the system.

--
Affected Systems:
All systems.

--
Attack Scenarios:
An attacker can search HTML files for comments, send unexpected requests to generate error messages or access to sensitive files.

--
Ease of Attack:
Simple.

--
False Positives:
None known.

--
False Negatives:
None known.

--
Corrective Action:
Ensure the system is using an up to date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied. Disallow access to sensitive files, remove any comments left in the user accessible code.
Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

--

name: SSRF attempt (127.x.x.x) - Dot-less decimal representation (Parameter)
description:
Summary:
This event is generated when an attempt is made to send crafted requests from the back-end server of a web application. This is a general attack detection signature (i.e. it is not specific to any web application).

Impact:
Successful exploitation will result in information gathering and system integrity compromise. Possible unauthorized administrative access to the server or application can result. Possible execution of arbitrary code of the attacker's choosing can result.

Detailed Information:
In a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) attack, the attacker can abuse functionality on the server to read or update internal resources. The attacker can supply or a modify a URL which the code running on the server will read or submit data to, and by carefully selecting the URLs, the attacker may be able to connect to internal services like http enabled databases or perform post requests towards internal services which are not intended to be exposed.

Affected Systems:
All systems.

Attack Scenarios:
An attacker can bypass security measures by using the back-end server to reach internal corporate servers, and send authenticated requests on behalf of the server.

Ease Of Attack:
Simple to medium.

False Positives:
Some applications may accept valid input which matches these signatures.

False Negatives:
None known.

Corrective Action:
Ensure the system is using an up to date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied. Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

This event is generated when an attempt is made to send crafted requests from the back-end server of a web application. This is a general attack detection signature (i.e. it is not specific to any web application).

Impact:
Successful exploitation will result in information gathering and system integrity compromise. Possible unauthorized administrative access to the server or application can result. Possible execution of arbitrary code of the attacker's choosing can result.

Detailed Information:
In a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) attack, the attacker can abuse functionality on the server to read or update internal resources. The attacker can supply or a modify a URL which the code running on the server will read or submit data to, and by carefully selecting the URLs, the attacker may be able to connect to internal services like http enabled databases or perform post requests towards internal services which are not intended to be exposed.

Affected Systems:
All systems.

Attack Scenarios:
An attacker can bypass security measures by using the back-end server to reach internal corporate servers, and send authenticated requests on behalf of the server.

Ease Of Attack:
Simple to medium.

False Positives:
Some applications may accept valid input which matches these signatures.

False Negatives:
None known.

Corrective Action:
Ensure the system is using an up to date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied. Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

Additional References:
https://www.owasp.org/index.php/Server_Side_Request_Forgery

description:
Summary:
This event is generated when an attempt is made to send crafted requests from the back-end server of a web application. This is a general attack detection signature (i.e. it is not specific to any web application).

Impact:
Successful exploitation will result in information gathering and system integrity compromise. Possible unauthorized administrative access to the server or application can result. Possible execution of arbitrary code of the attacker's choosing can result.

Detailed Information:
In a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) attack, the attacker can abuse functionality on the server to read or update internal resources. The attacker can supply or a modify a URL which the code running on the server will read or submit data to, and by carefully selecting the URLs, the attacker may be able to connect to internal services like http enabled databases or perform post requests towards internal services which are not intended to be exposed.

Affected Systems:
All systems.

Attack Scenarios:
An attacker can bypass security measures by using the back-end server to reach internal corporate servers, and send authenticated requests on behalf of the server.

Ease Of Attack:
Simple to medium.

False Positives:
Some applications may accept valid input which matches these signatures.

False Negatives:
None known.

Corrective Action:
Ensure the system is using an up to date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied. Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

Additional References:
https://www.owasp.org/index.php/Server_Side_Request_Forgery

name: WebLogic Server Core Insecure File Upload - DeploymentService
description:
Summary:
This event is generated when an attempt is made to upload files queries to the vulnerable web application. This is a general attack detection signature (i.e. it is not specific to any web application).

Impact:
Successful exploitation will result in information gathering and system integrity compromise. Possible unauthorized administrative access to the server or application can result. Possible execution of arbitrary code of the attacker's choosing can result.

Detailed Information:
Uploaded files represent a significant risk to applications. The first step in many attacks is to get some code to the system to be attacked. Then the attack only needs to find a way to get the code executed. Using a file upload helps the attacker accomplish the first step.

Affected Systems:
All systems.

Attack Scenarios:
An attacker may upload a file which can then be used as a web-shell to gain control of the web server.

Ease Of Attack:
Simple to medium.

False Positives:
None known.

False Negatives:
None known.

Corrective Action:
Restrict file upload only to verified and authenticated users. Prevent access from the web server to execute the uploaded file.

Additional References:
https://www.owasp.org/index.php/Unrestricted_File_Upload

This event is generated when an attempt is made to inject code into server-side templates on a vulnerable web application. This is a general attack detection signature (i.e. it is not specific to any web application).

Impact:
Successful exploitation will result in information gathering and system integrity compromise. Possible unauthorized administrative access to the server or application can result. Possible execution of arbitrary code of the attacker's choosing can result.

Detailed Information:
Template Injection can be used to directly attack web servers' internals and often obtain Remote Code Execution (RCE), turning every vulnerable application into a potential pivot point.

Affected Systems:
All systems with server-side template support are potentially affected.

Attack Scenarios:
An attacker can inject code snippets into the web application if user input is not correctly sanitized or checked before passing that input.

Ease Of Attack:
Simple to medium.

False Positives:
None known.

False Negatives:
None known.

Corrective Action:
Ensure the system is using an up to date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied. Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

Additional References:
https://www.owasp.org/index.php/Server-Side_Includes_(SSI)_Injection

description:
Summary:
Google Hacking Database (GHDB): 
Google hacking is a term that refers to the art of creating complex search engine queries in order to filter through large amounts of search results for information related to computer security. In its malicious format it can be used to detect websites that are vulnerable to numerous exploits and vulnerabilities as well as locate private, sensitive information about others, such as credit card numbers, social security numbers, and passwords.
[Source: Wikipedia]

This event is generated when an attempt is made to obtain sensitive information or a leakage has been detected. This is a general detection signature (i.e. it is not specific to any web application).

--
Impact:
Information disclosure.
The information may be sensitive itself (e.g. credit card numbers) or  may aid the attacker to mount a more dangerous attack (e.g. user or system passwords).

--
Detailed Information:
Sensitive information may be present within HTML comments, error messages, source code, or simply left in files which are accessible by remote clients.
This can lead to the disclosure of sensitive system information which may
be used by an attacker to further compromise the system.

--
Affected Systems:
All systems.

--
Attack Scenarios:
An attacker can search HTML files for comments, send unexpected requests to generate error messages or access to sensitive files.

--
Ease of Attack:
Simple.

--
False Positives:
None known.

--
False Negatives:
None known.

--
Corrective Action:
Ensure the system is using an up to date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied. Disallow access to sensitive files, remove any comments left in the user accessible code.
Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

--

name: Padding Oracle attack (Padbuster)
description:
Summary:
This signature is triggered when a string resembling the padding oracle attack is detected.

Impact:
Successful exploitation will result in information gathering and system integrity compromise.

Detailed Information:
The padding oracle attack attempts to decrypt a given ciphertext using the padding mechanism of CBC encryption, while inspecting system behavior.

Affected Systems:
All systems with user-provided encrypted values.

Attack Scenarios:
An attacker can discover private application data using this method.

Ease Of Attack:
Medium.

False Positives:
Some applications recieve legitimate input in a similar manner to that which the attack is executed.

False Negatives:
None known.

Corrective Action:
Make sure to update your system configuration to not expose application errors.

Additional References:
http://blog.gdssecurity.com/labs/2010/9/14/automated-padding-oracle-attacks-with-padbuster.html

name: Windows alternative data stream access (2)
description:
Summary:
This event is triggered when an attempt is made to access a file via an alternative data stream.

Impact:
Vary from information gathering to web server compromise.

Detailed Information:
A file on a DOS/Windows O/S may contain several data streams. The main data stream can be can be accessed via the ::$INDEX_ALLOCATION stream.

Affected Systems:
DOS/Windows file systems.

Attack Scenarios:
An attacker may use an alternative data stream to bypass enforcement based on a specific URL.

Ease Of Attack:
Simple.

False Positives:
A path that contains the string "::$INDEX_ALLOCATION" in it may trigger the event.

False Negatives:
None known.

Corrective Action:
Make sure that your web server is up to date and prevents access to files via an alternative data stream.
Make sure that all pages on your web site are evaluated for protection and not based only on a specific url list.

Additional References:
https://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/aa364404(v=vs.85).aspx

Summary:
This event is generated when an attempt is made to scan for vulnerabilities by security scanner. This is a general detection signature (i.e. it is not specific to any web application).

Impact:
Vary from information gathering to web server compromise.

Detailed Information:
This event is generated when an attempt is made to scan a web server or an application running on a web server for a possible vulnerability.

Affected Systems:
All systems.

Attack Scenarios:
There are many possible.

Ease Of Attack:
Simple to medium.

False Positives:
Some applications may accept valid input which matches these signatures.

False Negatives:
None known.

Corrective Action:
Ensure the system is using an up to date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied. Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

Additional References:
http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_application_security_scanner

name: Digest authentication uninitialized memory reflection
description:
Summary:
This event is generated when an attempt is made to exploit Apache Digest authentication uninitialized memory reflection vulnerability.

Impact:
Leakage of potentially confidential information, and a segfault leading to DoS.

Detailed Information:
The value placeholder in [Proxy-]Authorization headers of type 'Digest' was not initialized or reset before or between successive key=value assignments by mod_auth_digest. Providing an initial key with no '=' assignment could reflect the stale value of uninitialized pool memory used by the prior request.

Affected Systems:
Apache HTTP Server

Attack Scenarios:
An attacker may send a request containing a crafted Digest authorization header.

Ease Of Attack:
Simple to medium.

name: WordPress Simply Static Plugin Information Leakage
description:
Summary:
This event is generated when an attempt is made to access hidden web site content or functionality. This is a general detection signature (i.e. it is not specific to any web application).

Impact:
Information disclosure. This may aid the attacker to mount a more dangerous attack.

Detailed Information:
By making educated guesses, the attacker could discover hidden web site content and functionality, such as configuration, temporary, backup or sample files.This can lead to the disclosure of sensitive system information which maybe used by an attacker to further compromise the system.

Affected Systems:
All systems.

Attack Scenarios:
An attacker can search the web site for known sample files or files with .tmp, .bak and other extensions or attempt to access administrative pages or directories.

Ease Of Attack:
Simple.

False Positives:
Some applications may accept valid input which matches these signatures.

None known.

Corrective Action:
Ensure the system is using an up to date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied. Restrict access to sensitive files and nonpublic web server functionality. Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

This event is generated when an attempt is made to access hidden web site content or functionality. This is a general detection signature (i.e. it is not specific to any web application).

Impact:
Information disclosure. This may aid the attacker to mount a more dangerous attack.

Detailed Information:
By making educated guesses, the attacker could discover hidden web site content and functionality, such as configuration, temporary, backup or sample files.This can lead to the disclosure of sensitive system information which maybe used by an attacker to further compromise the system.

Affected Systems:
All systems.

Attack Scenarios:
An attacker can search the web site for known sample files or files with .tmp, .bak and other extensions or attempt to access administrative pages or directories.

Ease Of Attack:
Simple.

False Positives:
Some applications may accept valid input which matches these signatures.

False Negatives:
None known.

Corrective Action:
Ensure the system is using an up to date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied. Restrict access to sensitive files and nonpublic web server functionality. Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

Additional References:
http://www.webappsec.org/projects/threat/classes/predictable_resource_location.shtml

This event is generated when an attempt is made to access hidden web site content or functionality. This is a general detection signature (i.e. it is not specific to any web application).

Impact:
Information disclosure. This may aid the attacker to mount a more dangerous attack.

Detailed Information:
By making educated guesses, the attacker could discover hidden web site content and functionality, such as configuration, temporary, backup or sample files.This can lead to the disclosure of sensitive system information which maybe used by an attacker to further compromise the system.

Affected Systems:
All systems.

Attack Scenarios:
An attacker can search the web site for known sample files or files with .tmp, .bak and other extensions or attempt to access administrative pages or directories.

Ease Of Attack:
Simple.

False Positives:
Some applications may accept valid input which matches these signatures.

False Negatives:
None known.

Corrective Action:
Ensure the system is using an up to date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied. Restrict access to sensitive files and nonpublic web server functionality. Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

Additional References:
http://www.webappsec.org/projects/threat/classes/predictable_resource_location.shtml

This event is generated when an attempt is made to access hidden web site content or functionality. This is a general detection signature (i.e. it is not specific to any web application).

Impact:
Information disclosure. This may aid the attacker to mount a more dangerous attack.

Detailed Information:
By making educated guesses, the attacker could discover hidden web site content and functionality, such as configuration, temporary, backup or sample files.This can lead to the disclosure of sensitive system information which maybe used by an attacker to further compromise the system.

Affected Systems:
All systems.

Attack Scenarios:
An attacker can search the web site for known sample files or files with .tmp, .bak and other extensions or attempt to access administrative pages or directories.

Ease Of Attack:
Simple.

False Positives:
Some applications may accept valid input which matches these signatures.

False Negatives:
None known.

Corrective Action:
Ensure the system is using an up to date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied. Restrict access to sensitive files and nonpublic web server functionality. Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

Additional References:
http://www.webappsec.org/projects/threat/classes/predictable_resource_location.shtml

This event is generated when an attempt is made to access hidden web site content or functionality. This is a general detection signature (i.e. it is not specific to any web application).

Impact:
Information disclosure. This may aid the attacker to mount a more dangerous attack.

Detailed Information:
By making educated guesses, the attacker could discover hidden web site content and functionality, such as configuration, temporary, backup or sample files.This can lead to the disclosure of sensitive system information which maybe used by an attacker to further compromise the system.

Affected Systems:
All systems.

Attack Scenarios:
An attacker can search the web site for known sample files or files with .tmp, .bak and other extensions or attempt to access administrative pages or directories.

Ease Of Attack:
Simple.

False Positives:
Some applications may accept valid input which matches these signatures.

False Negatives:
None known.

Corrective Action:
Ensure the system is using an up to date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied. Restrict access to sensitive files and nonpublic web server functionality. Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

Additional References:
http://www.webappsec.org/projects/threat/classes/predictable_resource_location.shtml

This event is generated when an attempt is made to access hidden web site content or functionality. This is a general detection signature (i.e. it is not specific to any web application).

Impact:
Information disclosure. This may aid the attacker to mount a more dangerous attack.

Detailed Information:
By making educated guesses, the attacker could discover hidden web site content and functionality, such as configuration, temporary, backup or sample files.This can lead to the disclosure of sensitive system information which maybe used by an attacker to further compromise the system.

Affected Systems:
All systems.

Attack Scenarios:
An attacker can search the web site for known sample files or files with .tmp, .bak and other extensions or attempt to access administrative pages or directories.

Ease Of Attack:
Simple.

False Positives:
Some applications may accept valid input which matches these signatures.

False Negatives:
None known.

Corrective Action:
Ensure the system is using an up to date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied. Restrict access to sensitive files and nonpublic web server functionality. Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

Additional References:
http://www.webappsec.org/projects/threat/classes/predictable_resource_location.shtml

This event is generated when an attempt is made to execute a Path Traversal attack. This is a general attack detection signature (i.e. it is not specific to any web application).

--
Impact:
Information disclosure. This is a directory traversal attempt which can
lead to information disclosure and possible exposure of sensitive
system information.

--
Detailed Information:
Directory traversal attacks usually target web servers, web applications and ftp
servers that do not correctly check the path to a file when requested by
the client.
This can lead to the disclosure of sensitive system information which may
be used by an attacker to further compromise the system.

--
Affected Systems:
All systems.

--
Attack Scenarios:
An authorized user or anonymous user can use the directory traversal 
technique to browse folders outside the web server root directory. Information
gathered may be sensitive in and of itself, or used in further attacks against the host.

--
Ease of Attack:
Simple.

--
False Positives:
None known.

--
False Negatives:
None known.

--
Corrective Action:
Ensure the system is using an up to date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied.
Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

--
Additional References:

Path Traversal
http://www.webappsec.org/projects/threat/classes/path_traversal.shtml

--

name: Generic XPath injection attempt
description:
Summary:
This event is generated when an attempt is made to inject XPath queries to the vulnerable web application. This is a general attack detection signature (i.e. it is not specific to any web application).

Impact:
Successful exploitation will result in information gathering and system integrity compromise. Possible unauthorized administrative access to the server or application can result. Possible execution of arbitrary code of the attacker's choosing can result.

Detailed Information:
XPath-Injection occurs when a web application doesn't sanitize user-supplied input and places it directly into the XML document query.This event indicates that an attempt has been made by the client to inject XPath query into the application.

Affected Systems:
All systems with XML support are potentially affected.

Attack Scenarios:
An attacker can inject XPath queries to the web application if user input is not correctly sanitized or checked before passing that input.

Ease Of Attack:
Simple to medium.

False Positives:
Some free-text user input may match XPath Injection signatures.

False Negatives:
None known.

Corrective Action:
Ensure the system is using an up to date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied. Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

Additional References:
http://www.webappsec.org/projects/threat/classes/xpath_injection.shtml

Serious. Successful exploitation will result in information gathering and system integrity compromise. Possible modification of LDAP tree.

This event indicates that an attempt has been made to inject LDAP statement. If user supplied input is not correctly sanitized the attacker could change LDAP statement construction.

Affected Systems:
All systems with LDAP connectivity are potentially affected.

An attacker can inject LDAP queries to the backend LDAP server for an application if user input is not correctly sanitized or checked before passing that input to the LDAP server.

Simple to medium.

Some free-text user input may match LDAP Injection signatures.

False Negatives:
None known.

Ensure the system is using an up to date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied. Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

description:

An attacker can supply or invoke execution of OS commands via unsanitized input.

Medium to hard.

None known.

name: Apache Struts ClassLoader code injection
description:
Summary:
This signature is triggered when at attempt is made to exploit the Apache Struts ClassLoader manipulation vulnerability.

Impact:
Successful exploitation will result in information gathering and system integrity compromise. Possible unauthorized administrative access to the server or application can result. Possible execution of arbitrary code of the attacker's choosing can result.

Detailed Information:
The vulnerability allows an attacker to manipulate ClassLoader by using the 'class' parameter, which is directly mapped to the getClass() method through the ParametersInterceptor module in the Struts framework.

Affected Systems:
All systems with Apache Struts versions prior to 2.3.16.2 or prior to 1.3.10.

Attack Scenarios:
An attacker can execute Java code on a vulnerable machine, compromising the security of the entire system.

Ease Of Attack:
Simple to medium.

False Positives:
Some applications recieve legitimate input in a similar manner to that which the attack is executed.

False Negatives:
None known.

Corrective Action:
Make sure to upgrade your system to the latest version of Apache Struts.

Additional References:
http://devcentral.f5.com/articles/mitigating-the-apache-struts-classloader-manipulation-vulnerabilities-using-asm

This event is generated when an attempt is made to remotely execute an OS command. This is a general attack detection signature (i.e. it is not specific to any web application, but is dependent on the webserver Operating System).

Impact:
Serious. Execution of arbitrary commands may be possible.

Detailed Information:
Web application could be tricked to execute operating system command if user supplied input isn't properly checked. This event indicates that an attempt has been made to inject an operating system command from a remote machine via unvalidated input of web application.

Affected Systems:
All systems.

Attack Scenarios:
There are many possible.

Ease Of Attack:
Simple to medium.

False Positives:
Some applications may accept valid input which matches these signatures.

False Negatives:
None known.

Corrective Action:
Ensure the system is using an up to date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied. Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

Additional References:
http://www.webappsec.org/projects/threat/classes/os_commanding.shtml

This event is generated when an attempt is made to remotely execute an OS command. This is a general attack detection signature (i.e. it is not specific to any web application, but is dependent on the webserver Operating System).

Impact:
Serious. Execution of arbitrary commands may be possible.

Detailed Information:
Web application could be tricked to execute operating system command if user supplied input isn't properly checked. This event indicates that an attempt has been made to inject an operating system command from a remote machine via unvalidated input of web application.

Affected Systems:
All systems.

Attack Scenarios:
There are many possible.

Ease Of Attack:
Simple to medium.

False Positives:
Some applications may accept valid input which matches these signatures.

False Negatives:
None known.

Corrective Action:
Ensure the system is using an up to date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied. Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

Additional References:
http://www.webappsec.org/projects/threat/classes/os_commanding.shtml

name: Ghostscript Type Confusion Arbitrary Command Execution
description:

This event is triggered when at attempt is made to exploit Ghostscript 9.21 type confusion arbitrary command execution.

Impact:
Vary from information gathering to web server compromise.

Artifex Ghostscript through 2017-04-26 allows -dSAFER bypass and remote command execution via .rsdparams type confusion with a "/OutputFile (%pipe%" substring in a crafted .eps document that is an input to the gs program, as exploited in the wild in April 2017.

Ghostscript

There are many possible.

Simple to medium.

This event is generated when an attempt is made to remotely execute an OS command. This is a general attack detection signature (i.e. it is not specific to any web application, but is dependent on the webserver Operating System).

Impact:
Serious. Execution of arbitrary commands may be possible.

Detailed Information:
Web application could be tricked to execute operating system command if user supplied input isn't properly checked.This event indicates that an attempt has been made to inject an operating system command from a remote machine via unvalidated input of web application.

Affected Systems:
Unix/Linux

Attack Scenarios:
An attacker can supply or invoke execution of OS commands via unsanitized input.

Ease Of Attack:
Vary from simple to medium.

False Positives:
Some free-text user input may match Command Execution signatures.

False Negatives:
None known.

Corrective Action:
Ensure the system is using an up-to-date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied. Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

This event is generated when an attempt is made to remotely execute an OS command. This is a general attack detection signature (i.e. it is not specific to any web application, but is dependent on the webserver Operating System).

Impact:
Serious. Execution of arbitrary commands may be possible.

Detailed Information:
Web application could be tricked to execute operating system command if user supplied input isn't properly checked.This event indicates that an attempt has been made to inject an operating system command from a remote machine via unvalidated input of web application.

Affected Systems:
Microsoft Windows

Attack Scenarios:
An attacker can supply or invoke execution of OS commands via unsanitized input.

Ease Of Attack:
Vary from simple to medium.

False Positives:
Some free-text user input may match Command Execution signatures.

False Negatives:
None known.

Corrective Action:
Ensure the system is using an up-to-date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied. Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

This event is generated when an attempt is made to remotely execute an OS command. This is a general attack detection signature (i.e. it is not specific to any web application, but is dependent on the webserver Operating System).

Impact:
Serious. Execution of arbitrary commands may be possible.

Detailed Information:
Web application could be tricked to execute operating system command if user supplied input isn't properly checked.This event indicates that an attempt has been made to inject an operating system command from a remote machine via unvalidated input of web application.

Affected Systems:
Microsoft Windows

Attack Scenarios:
An attacker can supply or invoke execution of OS commands via unsanitized input.

Ease Of Attack:
Vary from simple to medium.

False Positives:
Some free-text user input may match Command Execution signatures.

False Negatives:
None known.

Corrective Action:
Ensure the system is using an up-to-date version of the software and has had all vendor supplied patches applied. Utilize "Positive Security Model" by accepting only known types of input in web application.

name: TCPDF Library Arbitrary File Deletion
description:
Summary:
TCPDF library is one of the world's most used open source PHP libraries, included in thousands of CMS and Web applications worldwide.

Impact:
Vary from information gathering to web server compromise.

Detailed Information:
The identified payload allows to exploit any POI vulnerable web application that uses unserialize() on not sanitized user input in a point from which the Tcpdf class is loadable. The payload abuses the __destruct() magic method of the Tcpdf class defined in tcpdf.php and allows to arbitrary delete files on the filesystem.

Affected Systems:
PHP

Attack Scenarios:
There are many possible.

Ease Of Attack:
Simple to medium.

False Positives:
None known.

False Negatives:
None known.

Corrective Action:
Upgrade your TCPDF library to version > 5.9

Additional References:
http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TCPDF
